accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)?
o: A statutory body under the IRDA Act, 1999, regulating insurance and reinsurance companies
A constitutional body regulating only life insurance
A statutory body under the SEBI Act, 1992, regulating pension funds
A non-statutory body under the Companies Act, 2013, regulating banks
accepted.x: IRDAI is a statutory body constituted under the IRDA Act, 1999. It is the apex regulator of insurance and reinsurance companies.
accepted.tq: Use the establishing Act and regulated sector to eliminate swapped-body options.
accepted.sec: IRDAI - statutory basis, recommending committee, year, sector regulated, expert panels

accepted.s: The opening of the insurance sector to private participation was associated with which legislation?
o: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority Act, 1999
Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority Act, 2013
Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992
accepted.x: The IRDA Act, 1999 opened the insurance sector to private participation and provided the statutory basis for IRDAI.
accepted.tq: Match the reform outcome with the correct establishing legislation.
accepted.sec: IRDAI - statutory basis, recommending committee, year, sector regulated, expert panels

accepted.s: The establishment of IRDAI was recommended by the:
accepted.x: The Malhotra Committee recommended insurance-sector reforms that led to the establishment of IRDAI. The Gadgil Committee is the confusable but incorrect option here.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between similarly placed committees by linking the Malhotra Committee with insurance reforms.
accepted.sec: IRDAI - statutory basis, recommending committee, year, sector regulated, expert panels

accepted.s: IRDAI was set up in:
accepted.x: IRDAI was set up in April 2000 under the statutory framework created by the IRDA Act, 1999.
accepted.tq: Use the year sequence carefully: the Act preceded the setting up of the regulator.
accepted.sec: IRDAI - statutory basis, recommending committee, year, sector regulated, expert panels

accepted.s: Under which provision does IRDAI frame regulations for the insurance industry?
accepted.x: IRDAI frames regulations for the insurance industry under Section 114A of the Insurance Act, 1938. Section 16A of the IRDA Act concerns the Policyholders' Education and Protection Fund.
accepted.tq: Separate provisions by matching each section with its statute and subject.
accepted.sec: IRDAI - statutory basis, recommending committee, year, sector regulated, expert panels

accepted.s: The IRDAI panel on a standard cyber liability insurance product was chaired by:
accepted.x: The IRDAI expert panel on a standard cyber liability insurance product was chaired by P. Umesh.
accepted.tq: Identify the person directly associated with the specialised expert panel.
accepted.sec: IRDAI - statutory basis, recommending committee, year, sector regulated, expert panels

accepted.s:
With reference to the Sabka Bima Sabki Raksha (Amendment of Insurance Laws) Act, 2025, consider the following statements:
1. It allows up to 100% foreign direct investment in insurance companies.
2. It amends the Insurance Act, 1938, the LIC Act, 1956 and the IRDA Act, 1999.
3. It was passed on 17 December 2025.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Act passed on 17 December 2025 permits up to 100% FDI in insurance companies and amends the three specified laws.
accepted.tq: Check the date, FDI limit and complete set of amended Acts together.
accepted.sec: IRDAI - statutory basis, recommending committee, year, sector regulated, expert panels

accepted.s: IRDAI operationalised the Policyholders' Education and Protection Fund in:
accepted.x: IRDAI operationalised the Policyholders' Education and Protection Fund in July 2026.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the enactment date from the later operationalisation date.
accepted.sec: IRDAI - statutory basis, recommending committee, year, sector regulated, expert panels

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT a measure included in the package associated with operationalisation of the Policyholders' Education and Protection Fund?
o: Revision of actuarial and investment rules
Mandatory tagging of an authorised salesperson to each policy
Perpetual licensing of intermediaries with an annual fee
Abolition of licensing requirements for intermediaries
accepted.x: The package made an authorised salesperson mandatory for each policy, introduced perpetual licensing with an annual fee for intermediaries, and revised actuarial and investment rules. It did not abolish licensing requirements.
accepted.tq: Find the option that reverses the stated regulatory reform.
accepted.sec: IRDAI - statutory basis, recommending committee, year, sector regulated, expert panels

accepted.s: Which accounting standards replaced IGAAP for insurers?
accepted.x: Ind AS 117 and Ind AS 109 replaced IGAAP for insurers, and IRDAI enforces their adoption.
accepted.tq: Pair the exact accounting standards with the insurance-sector transition.
accepted.sec: IRDAI - statutory basis, recommending committee, year, sector regulated, expert panels

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the Domestic Systemically Important Insurers for FY 2025–26?
o: General Insurance Corporation of India Re
accepted.x: The Domestic Systemically Important Insurers for FY 2025–26 are LIC, GIC Re and New India Assurance. HDFC Bank is listed among the D-SIBs, not the D-SIIs.
accepted.tq: Separate systemically important insurers from systemically important banks.
accepted.sec: IRDAI - statutory basis, recommending committee, year, sector regulated, expert panels

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Regulator)
 a. RBI
 b. IRDAI
 c. IBBI
 d. IFSCA

List-II (Establishing Act)
 i. Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016
 ii. IRDA Act, 1999
 iii. RBI Act, 1934
 iv. IFSCA Act, 2019

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
accepted.x: RBI is established under the RBI Act, 1934; IRDAI under the IRDA Act, 1999; IBBI under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016; and IFSCA under the IFSCA Act, 2019.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure Act–regulator pairs and eliminate codes containing a mismatch.
accepted.sec: Regulator → establishing Act and date set up

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: The RBI was set up on 1 April 1935 and was nationalised in 1949. PFRDA became statutory from 2014, IBBI was set up on 1 October 2016, and IFSCA on 27 April 2020.
accepted.tq: Use the date and status together; the distractors swap dates among regulators.
accepted.sec: Regulator → establishing Act and date set up

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. SEBI was set up as a non-statutory body on 12 April 1988.
2. SEBI received statutory powers on 30 January 1992.
3. SEBI became autonomous or statutory from 12 April 1992.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct for the chronology of SEBI's institutional development. The dates distinguish its initial non-statutory existence, statutory powers and later autonomous or statutory status.
accepted.tq: Arrange institutional milestones by reading each date and status precisely.
accepted.sec: Regulator → establishing Act and date set up

accepted.s: PFRDA was initially constituted as an interim body by resolution in 2003 and became statutory from:
accepted.x: PFRDA was constituted as an interim body by resolution in 2003 and became statutory from 2014 under the PFRDA Act, 2013.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the interim-body year from the year in which statutory status began.
accepted.sec: Regulator → establishing Act and date set up

accepted.s:
Which of the following chronological sequences is correct?
A. RBI is set up
B. SEBI is set up as a non-statutory body
C. IBBI is set up
D. IFSCA is set up
accepted.x: The correct sequence is RBI in 1935, SEBI as a non-statutory body in 1988, IBBI in 2016 and IFSCA in 2020.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the intermediate regulator.
accepted.sec: Regulator → establishing Act and date set up

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: IBBI — New Delhi — Ministry of Finance
PFRDA — New Delhi — Ministry of Finance
accepted.x: IBBI is headquartered in New Delhi but comes under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, not the Ministry of Finance. The other pairs are correctly matched.
accepted.tq: Check the parent ministry rather than relying only on the headquarters.
accepted.sec: Regulator → headquarters and parent ministry

accepted.s: The headquarters of the International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA) is located at:
accepted.x: IFSCA is headquartered at GIFT City, Gandhinagar. It functions under the Ministry of Finance.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive headquarters location to separate IFSCA from the Mumbai- and Delhi-based regulators.
accepted.sec: Regulator → headquarters and parent ministry

accepted.s: Which regulator has regional offices in New Delhi, Kolkata, Chennai and Ahmedabad in addition to its headquarters?
accepted.x: SEBI is headquartered in Mumbai and has regional offices in New Delhi, Kolkata, Chennai and Ahmedabad.
accepted.tq: Match the complete regional-office pattern with the correct regulator.
accepted.sec: Regulator → headquarters and parent ministry

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Ministry of Finance nominates representatives to the boards of SEBI, IRDAI and RBI.
2. IBBI is under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.
3. IFSCA is under the Ministry of Finance.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Ministry of Finance nominates representatives to the boards of SEBI, IRDAI and RBI; IBBI belongs to Corporate Affairs, while IFSCA belongs to Finance.
accepted.tq: Compare parent ministries and board-nomination authority without reversing institutional relationships.
accepted.sec: Regulator → headquarters and parent ministry

accepted.s: Which of the following is associated with IFSCA?
o: Promotion of FinTech and regulatory and innovation sandboxes
Issue of the one-rupee currency note
Management of the Public Debt Office
accepted.x: IFSCA promotes FinTech as well as regulatory and innovation sandboxes. The other functions belong to RBI or IRDAI-related domains.
accepted.tq: Identify the regulator from the function rather than from its location alone.
accepted.sec: Regulator → headquarters and parent ministry

accepted.s: The Monetary Policy Committee of the RBI is a statutory body consisting of:
o: Six members, all external members appointed by the Centre
Seven members, including four from the RBI and three from the Finance Ministry
Six members, including three from the RBI and three external members appointed by the Centre
Five members, all appointed by the RBI Governor
accepted.x: The MPC is a statutory six-member body under the RBI Act, 1934. It has three RBI members and three external members appointed by the Centre.
accepted.tq: Use the composition split to reject wrong strength and appointing-authority claims.
accepted.sec: RBI - Monetary Policy Committee, banker/regulator functions, inflation-targeting mandate

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the RBI Governor's position in the Monetary Policy Committee?
o: The Governor is a member without voting rights
The Governor is the chair and has a casting vote
The Governor appoints all three external members and has no casting vote
The Governor is nominated by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs
accepted.x: The RBI Governor chairs the MPC and has a casting vote. The three external members are appointed by the Centre.
accepted.tq: Ask who performs the role and who holds the deciding power.
accepted.sec: RBI - Monetary Policy Committee, banker/regulator functions, inflation-targeting mandate

accepted.s: The external members of the Monetary Policy Committee are appointed by the Centre for a period of:
accepted.x: The three external members of the MPC are appointed by the Centre for four years.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the four-year tenure from the five-year inflation-target cycle.
accepted.sec: RBI - Monetary Policy Committee, banker/regulator functions, inflation-targeting mandate

accepted.s: Under the inflation-targeting framework, the inflation target is set by the Centre in consultation with the RBI once every:
accepted.x: Under Section 45ZA, the Centre, in consultation with the RBI, sets the inflation target every five years.
accepted.tq: Separate the five-year target-setting cycle from the four-year MPC external-member tenure.
accepted.sec: RBI - Monetary Policy Committee, banker/regulator functions, inflation-targeting mandate

accepted.s: The inflation target under India's flexible inflation-targeting framework is:
o: 6% headline CPI with no tolerance band
4% CPI-Combined with a tolerance band of plus or minus 2%
2% CPI-Combined with a tolerance band of plus or minus 4%
4% WPI with a tolerance band of plus or minus 2%
accepted.x: The target is 4% CPI-Combined with a tolerance band of plus or minus 2%. The framework uses CPI-Combined, not WPI, as the specified measure.
accepted.tq: Check both the central target and the inflation measure before accepting the option.
accepted.sec: RBI - Monetary Policy Committee, banker/regulator functions, inflation-targeting mandate

accepted.s: Which index is described as the nominal anchor for inflation targeting, with base year 2024?
accepted.x: Headline CPI, with base year 2024, is the nominal anchor for the inflation-targeting framework.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the named nominal anchor from other economy-wide price indices.
accepted.sec: RBI - Monetary Policy Committee, banker/regulator functions, inflation-targeting mandate

accepted.s: If the inflation band is breached for three consecutive quarters, the RBI is required to report to the Centre under:
accepted.x: Section 45ZN requires the RBI to report to the Centre when the inflation band is breached for three consecutive quarters. The report must state the reasons, remedial actions and the time required to restore inflation.
accepted.tq: Match the exceptional reporting trigger with the correct statutory section.
accepted.sec: RBI - Monetary Policy Committee, banker/regulator functions, inflation-targeting mandate

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly states the hierarchy of objectives under the inflation-targeting framework?
o: Price stability is primary and growth is secondary
Growth is primary and price stability is secondary
Fiscal consolidation is primary and price stability is optional
Exchange-rate stability is primary and growth is excluded
accepted.x: Price stability is the primary objective, while growth is treated as a secondary objective.
accepted.tq: Identify the stated priority rather than selecting a neighbouring macroeconomic objective.
accepted.sec: RBI - Monetary Policy Committee, banker/regulator functions, inflation-targeting mandate

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a function of the Reserve Bank of India?
o: Regulating and supervising banks and NBFCs
Issuing the one-rupee note and coins
accepted.x: The Ministry of Finance issues the one-rupee note and coins. RBI functions include monetary authority, foreign-exchange management under FEMA, and regulation and supervision of banks and NBFCs.
accepted.tq: Find the exception by separating RBI's currency function from the one-rupee and coin issuing authority.
accepted.sec: RBI - Monetary Policy Committee, banker/regulator functions, inflation-targeting mandate

accepted.s: The RBI acts as banker and debt manager to the Government mainly through its:
accepted.x: The RBI performs its banker and debt-manager function to the Government through its Public Debt Office.
accepted.tq: Match the government-debt management function with the specialised RBI office.
accepted.sec: RBI - Monetary Policy Committee, banker/regulator functions, inflation-targeting mandate

accepted.s: The Public Debt Management Cell was set up primarily to:
o: issue all currency notes and coins
reduce the RBI's conflict of interest between monetary policy and debt management
accepted.x: The Public Debt Management Cell was established to reduce the RBI's conflict of interest between conducting monetary policy and managing public debt.
accepted.tq: Infer the institutional purpose from the conflict that the body was designed to address.
accepted.sec: RBI - Monetary Policy Committee, banker/regulator functions, inflation-targeting mandate

accepted.s: The RBI's May 2025 regulation-making framework emphasised:
o: privatisation of currency issue and abolition of supervision
accepted.x: The RBI's May 2025 regulation-making framework emphasised transparency, consultation and periodic review.
accepted.tq: Select the option containing the complete set of stated regulatory principles.
accepted.sec: RBI - Monetary Policy Committee, banker/regulator functions, inflation-targeting mandate

accepted.s: Which of the following is included among the Domestic Systemically Important Banks listed for the relevant period?
accepted.x: The D-SIBs listed are SBI, ICICI Bank and HDFC Bank. LIC, GIC Re and New India Assurance are identified as Domestic Systemically Important Insurers.
accepted.tq: Separate the banking and insurance categories before identifying the institution.
accepted.sec: RBI - Monetary Policy Committee, banker/regulator functions, inflation-targeting mandate

accepted.s:
With reference to the Upper-Layer NBFCs for 2026–27, consider the following statements:
1. Seventeen Upper-Layer NBFCs were named.
2. Tata Sons was included among them.
3. The entities must list within three years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: 17 Upper-Layer NBFCs were named for 2026–27, Tata Sons was among them, and they must list within three years.
accepted.tq: Verify the count, named example and compliance deadline as one regulatory package.
accepted.sec: RBI - Monetary Policy Committee, banker/regulator functions, inflation-targeting mandate
